name: Commissuroplasty

card.summary: Surgery that widens the mouth by moving the corners (oral commissures) outward, used by people who want a wider smile and lip line.
card.aka: mouth corner surgery, lateral commissuroplasty, mouth widening
card.note: Permanent scarring at the lip corners is the main reported concern; few surgeons offer it for cosmetic widening.

quick.overview:
Commissuroplasty reshapes the corners of the mouth. In cosmetic use it extends the commissures sideways so the lips are wider, which proponents say balances the lower face and widens the smile. Surgeons use the same technique in reconstruction after burns and other injuries.

The appearance payoff is a longer lip line relative to the face. Published research mostly covers reconstructive cases such as burn scarring and microstomia; cosmetic widening appears mainly in forum discussions and surgeon portfolios.
quick.how: It is done as an operation by a surgeon, sometimes alongside a lip lift. Forum members describe looking for surgeons who perform lateral commissuroplasty, comparing before-and-after photos and asking about scars and recovery. Makeup that visually extends the lip corners is discussed as a non-surgical alternative.
quick.risks: The cut and sutured corners leave scars at a highly visible, mobile spot, and members specifically ask about avoiding visible scarring. As with any facial surgery there are risks of infection, asymmetry and unsatisfactory shape. Forum posters note it is an uncommon procedure and that surgeons offering it are hard to find.

lead: Commissuroplasty is a surgical procedure on the oral commissures, the corners where the upper and lower lips meet. The same word covers reconstructive work, such as releasing scar contracture that has narrowed the mouth after a burn, and cosmetic lateral widening of a mouth the patient finds too narrow.[1][2]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to lengthen the lip line. One looksmax.org overview defines mouth width as the distance between the commissures and suggests considering it only after addressing maxilla, teeth and lip tonicity; it also covers makeup options that visually widen the mouth.[3] Another poster says their corners should align with the medial borders of the irises and fall a few millimetres short, and asks for examples of acceptable scarring.[4]

Published literature is dominated by reconstructive indications; little has been published on purely cosmetic widening.[1][2][6] The word also names unrelated operations on heart valves, where surgeons use commissuroplasty to repair the junctions between valve leaflets.[7]

angle.text: Cosmetic commissuroplasty is used to lengthen the lip line by moving the mouth corners laterally. People who feel their mouth is narrow relative to their face seek it to change proportions; non-surgical makeup techniques aim at the same look temporarily.

paras: The oral commissures are the points at each side of the mouth where the vermilion of the upper and lower lips meets. Commissuroplasty alters their position or the tissue around them. Lateral commissuroplasty moves the corner outward to lengthen the mouth, while related procedures can change the corner's height.[3]
In reconstruction the aim is function: restoring mouth opening, speech and eating in people whose mouths were narrowed by caustic ingestion or electrical burns.[1][2]

Microstomia, an abnormally small mouth opening, can be congenital, as in Freeman-Sheldon syndrome, or acquired through scarring from facial burns or systemic scleroderma. Wikipedia lists surgical scar release with grafting or repositioning among its treatments, together with prevention appliances, compression garments and exercises supervised by a speech or occupational therapist.[6]

Reconstructive teams also use commissuroplasty after cancer surgery. A 2023 paper in Head & Neck describes the technique with a triangular cheek flap in patients whose through-and-through cheek defects were rebuilt with free flaps.[8] These applications are where the surgical vocabulary and techniques used by cosmetic patients originate, and where most published outcome data sit.

Forum members treat mouth width as one proportion among lip features such as philtrum height, Cupid's bow and lip curvature. The overview thread sets out lip terminology and notes that orthodontic or jaw issues may be involved in lip appearance, which it says should be considered first.[3]

Posters ask where cosmetic lateral commissuroplasty can be obtained. One person seeking both a lip lift and lateral commissuroplasty says they could not find a surgeon in Europe who would combine them, that the procedure appears uncommon, and that they hope to avoid 'joker scars'; they mention seeing results by Dr Eppley.[5]
Makeup is the non-surgical route discussed alongside surgery: techniques that draw the lip line outward to create the look of a wider mouth.[3]

The overview thread frames lip aesthetics as a set of measurable relationships: mid-philtrum height and commissure height should be roughly equal in an adult with lips lightly in contact, and a mismatch produces an upper lip line the thread calls an inverted arc, a point it attributes to the orthodontist Farhad Naini.[3] It ties lip width and curvature to palate width, maxillary projection and tooth position, which is why its author lists orthognathic and orthodontic work first.[3] A second poster suggests the corners should align with the medial borders of the irises as a width guide.[4]

No studies found on purely cosmetic mouth widening. Reconstructive studies exist: a retrospective comparison of 29 children with perioral electrical burns found that commissuroplasty improved appearance compared with no treatment, but a splint alone gave the best cosmetic result and commissuroplasty scored similarly to no splint or surgery on overall scar involvement.[2] A 2026 systematic review and institutional series on caustic ingestion-induced microstomia reported heterogeneous techniques and 18 commissuroplasties in 11 patients using scar release, flaps, grafts and intraoral appliances.[1]

Forum discussion centres on scarring at the corners, given how visible and mobile the area is, and on finding an experienced surgeon.[4][5] Reconstructive literature describes the difficulty of keeping the new corner open without scar contracture, which is why splints and appliances feature in those protocols.[1][2]

timeline.event: A retrospective comparison of 29 children with perioral electrical burns evaluates commissuroplasty against splinting and no treatment.[2]
Head & Neck reports commissuroplasty with a triangular cheek flap after free-flap reconstruction of buccal defects.[8]
A systematic review and 11-patient institutional series on caustic-ingestion microstomia reports 18 commissuroplasties.[1]

lore.intro: Commissuroplasty appears on looksmax.org as an uncommon surgery that members research carefully before considering.[3][4][5]

claims.claim: A wider mouth is a proportion improvement worth surgery
claims.believers: Posters say the commissures should line up with the medial iris borders and that mouths falling short look narrow.[4]
claims.experts: No published studies have evaluated cosmetic mouth widening; the literature covers reconstruction after burns.[1][2]

claims.claim: Jaw, teeth and lip tonicity should be addressed before widening the mouth
claims.believers: The overview thread says maxilla projection, palate width, teeth and lip tonicity are related and come first.[3]
claims.experts: No studies compare these sequences for aesthetic outcomes.

claims.claim: Makeup can imitate a wider mouth without surgery
claims.believers: The same thread includes makeup options for the look of a wider mouth.[3]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested this.

claims.claim: Cosmetic commissuroplasty can be done with acceptable scarring
claims.believers: Posters ask for examples of acceptable scars and praise individual surgeon results they have seen, while hoping to avoid conspicuous 'joker scars'.[4][5]
claims.experts: Reconstructive papers report scar contracture as a central problem at the commissure and use splints, flaps and appliances to manage it; no study reports cosmetic scar outcomes.[1][2]
